card.name: Has after C. difficile diarrhea (CDAD)
card.fires_on: The word "has" right after "Clostridium (or Clostridioides) difficile associated diarrhea (CDAD)" in the standard antibiotic warning sentence. Rarely, it fires on a comma or a space before a number in other label text.

modes.label: CDAD warning sentence
modes.description: The verb "has" following the abbreviation (CDAD) at the start of the "has been reported with use of nearly all antibacterial agents" statement.
modes.example: Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea (CDAD)<< has>> been reported with use of nearly all antib

modes.label: Stray punctuation or spacing
modes.description: A comma or a space before a number in a study description, seen only occasionally.
modes.example: in clinical trials of 29-week duration, a decrease to subnormal levels of previously normal serum vitamin B 12 levels was observed in approximately<< >>7% of metformin-treated patients

card.writes: It lowers hedging words like "probably" and "likely", which fits a flat factual statement that comes next.
card.plain: It marks the fixed warning line that C. difficile diarrhea has been reported with nearly all antibiotics.
